clips.full: Barry looks up at a television above the camera and says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Another boat last night. Where are they all going to live? 'Cause it ain't round here. I can't afford round here. Both his hands stay round the mug the whole time; the phone stays on the table. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

The woman at the front and the people around her chant the same short sentence across the barrier together, twice, fists punching the air on every word. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, no motion blur, normal speed. Sound: an angry crowd chanting, rain. No music. Thanks.

Barry and the people around him shout back across the barrier, one short sentence, Barry shaking the sign on the last word, the man in the cap beside him jabbing his finger. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, no motion blur, normal speed. Sound: an angry crowd shouting back, rain. No music. Thanks.

The woman shouts one short sentence through the megaphone, twice, the megaphone staying at her mouth the whole time; around her, fists punch the air and the crowd roars. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, no motion blur, normal speed. Sound: a big crowd roaring and whistling in the rain, no clear words. No music. Thanks.

Barry shouts one short sentence through the megaphone, the megaphone staying at his mouth the whole time; the woman beside him shakes the sign, the man in the cap jabs his finger, the crowd roars. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, no motion blur, normal speed. Sound: a big crowd roaring and booing in the rain, no clear words. No music. Thanks.

Barry looks up from his phone and says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Nine hundred quid. For a box room. The phone stays low in his hand the whole time. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Denise looks across at Barry and says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Mine's gone up again. The café and the flat. Her hand stays flat on the cloth on the counter. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Denise looks across at Barry and says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: It's not the boats, Barry. It's the landlord. Put mine up twice this year. And the council's put my rates up for the privilege. Her hand stays flat on the cloth on the counter. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Denise looks across at Barry and says, deadpan, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Your daughter's right. She still lives with you. Her hand stays flat on the cloth on the counter. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Denise, not looking up, says, in a dry, flat northern English accent: Bloody landlord. Her hand stays flat on the cloth on the counter. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: her voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Barry, holding up the little Freddo, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Least something's still cheap. The Freddo stays in his hand the whole time. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

Barry, staring at the price card, says, in a gruff, flat, working-class south-east English accent: Twenty p? Bloody boats. His hands stay where they are. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, normal speed. Sound: his voice, cutlery and a radio murmuring in a small café. No music. Thanks.

A thin curl of steam drifts slowly up across the bottom of the frame; nothing else moves. Fixed camera, one continuous shot, sharp in every frame, no motion blur, normal speed. Sound: a small café, cutlery, a radio murmuring, rain outside. No people, no dialogue. No music. Thanks.
